idea: How to maintain a home water system
title: Checking Home Water Pressure
description: High static water pressure can silently damage faucet cartridges, toilet valves, and flexible supply lines. Testing water pressure at an outdoor hose bib is one of the most effective preventive maintenance checks a homeowner or apprentice can perform. Thread a dedicated pressure gauge onto an exterior hose spigot and open the valve completely to read the static pressure. Most residential plumbing systems are designed to operate safely between 40 and 80 PSI, though local code and manufacturer specifications govern exact limits. If your reading exceeds 80 PSI, your pressure-reducing valve (PRV) may need adjustment or replacement. What static pressure reading do you normally see on your residential service jobs?
